Title: Long-Lived Programmatic IAM Access Keys
Observation: Routine administration uses a long-lived IAM access key
Risk_If_Failed: Stolen key permits persistent unauthorized cloud access over the public internet network plane
Existing_Control: Virtual MFA is active on the user profile for console logins
Recommendation: Replace routine long-lived keys with federated temporary sessions via IAM Identity Center, then disable and remove the old key after validation
Retest_Method: Verify credential report shows zero active access keys for the identity
Notes: Persistent access keys stored on local development machines introduce exposure risk if a laptop is compromised

Title: Missing Account-Level Access Analyzer
Observation: No account-level external-access analyzer is active in the primary Region
Risk_If_Failed: Unintended external or cross-account resource sharing may remain unidentified on the network perimeter
Existing_Control: Global S3 account public access block is fully enabled
Recommendation: Evaluate and enable an account-level external access analyzer after ownership and current pricing are confirmed
Retest_Method: Run list-analyzers CLI check to confirm an active ACCOUNT-level analyzer exists
Notes: Without active analyzers, visibility into unintended cross-account resource access depends on manual point-in-time reviews

Title: Missing Multi-Region CloudTrail Trail
Observation: No ongoing multi-Region trail delivers management events to long-term storage
Risk_If_Failed: Investigation and retention needs exceed the rolling 90-day regional event-history window during an incident
Existing_Control: 90-day regional Event History remains enabled natively on the console plane
Recommendation: Design and deploy one protected multi-Region trail with global service events, log file integrity validation, and secure S3 retention
Retest_Method: Execute describe-trails CLI check to verify a multi-region trail is actively capturing events
Notes: Relying on default Event History leaves the organization blind to historical threat activity once the 90-day retention window closes

Title: Missing High-Risk Event Alerting Matrix
Observation: No repeatable alert or manual review exists for high-risk AWS changes
Risk_If_Failed: Root, IAM, S3, trail, or KMS key mutations remain undetected across active environments
Existing_Control: None; changes depend on manual ad-hoc log lookups
Recommendation: Implement priority high-risk event monitoring rules in Hosted Splunk and establish a daily manual fallback review procedure with escalation paths
Retest_Method: Trigger a test non-destructive high-risk management event and verify an alert reaches the security owner inside SLA thresholds
Notes: Gaps in active telemetry alerting prevent real-time incident containment, increasing attacker persistence capabilities inside the tenant workspace
